title: Customer signal cascades and rollback plays — May 2026
body:
TL;DR: Quick synthesis of recent customer threads where small changes cascade into multiple downstream support incidents. Two high-level themes: (1) private deployment onboarding friction -> customers opt for Hosted or delay adoption, (2) light-weight API changes (defaults, tokenization, batching) create subtle QoS regressions across webhooks and cached prompts.

What this doc is: quick operational playbook + short list of small-bet fixes we can ship this quarter to blunt the most frequent cascades. Not final — meant for CS/SE/Product pairing to riff on, test, and schedule.

Observed patterns (raw):
- New private deployments: network config + KMS key rotation timing -> >2 incidents in last 30 days; common thread: deploys that restrict egress to only corp CIDR cause auth/timeouts during container init.
- Model pinning + autoscaler mismatch: customers pin model:v2.1 but autoscaler scale-down removes pooling nodes -> first 50 requests see 2–3s cold-start blips then fallback to slower variant; customer perceives instability.
- Tokenization drift: updater that changed whitespace normalization interacts with client-side prompt templates -> short hallucination regressions in 3 customers, hard to reproduce locally.
- Batching/config defaults: changing default batch window from 20ms to 50ms reduced throughput variance but increased tail latency; webhooks with 1s user-visible timeout hit errors.
- Observability gaps: teams often file tickets with symptom but no route/model id; tracing requires opt-in which many customers haven't enabled.

Representative customer quotes (sanitized):
- "We got a spike in timeouts after your last release; our webhook queue filled and events dropped. We had to fallback to a smaller model to stay online." — fintech customer
- "Private install kept failing key rotation — engineer had to open a ticket and we spent 4 hours troubleshooting network egress rules." — regulated healthcare customer

Heatmap (frequency x severity) — shorthand:
- High frequency, high severity: observability gaps around route/model id; leads to long MTTR.
- High frequency, medium severity: defaults that touch batching/latency; many customers adapt but some with strict SLAs break.
- Low frequency, high severity: KMS/on-prem edgecases; big impact for individual customers.

Top actionable asks (ranked by expected impact / implementation effort):
1) "auto-telemetry-hints" (small-bet): If a request fails and tracing is off, include a one-click help header in error payload that instructs how to enable trace and collect route/model id. Low dev effort; high impact for CS triage.
2) "pin-safe-autoscale" (medium): When a customer pins a model version, autoscaler avoids aggressive scale-to-zero for grace window (configurable). Requires autoscaler + orchestration change; prevents cold-start cascades.
3) "egress-checker" (small): lightweight pre-deploy network sanity check for Private that validates KMS endpoints and known outbound control plane endpoints. Simple script + console UX.
4) "batch-window-aware-timeouts" (small): detect downstream webhooks with tight timeouts and auto-suggest batch-window downshift or provide per-route override.
5) "tokenization-compatibility-mode" (medium): opt-in compatibility toggle that uses previous whitespace normalization for pinned routes to avoid drift.
6) "default-observability-onboarding" (policy): turn on minimal request identifiers by default for new tenants (with clear privacy notice).

Rollback / mitigation plays (for CS + SE on-call):
- If multiple customers report similar tail-latency increases after a change: perform immediate config rollback for batch-window and pin-safe-autoscale gate; notify customers in affected cohort via console banner and CS email.
- For private deployment KMS/network errors: provide an "egress-checker" script via support reply and escalate to infra on-call if deployment failed during init phase.
- For tokenization regressions: quick toggle in route config to revert to prior normalization; route-level canary to 1% to verify.

Experimentation calendar (next 8 weeks):
- Week 1–2: implement auto-telemetry-hints in error responses; A/B test with 10% of failing requests, measure mean time to first response from customer.
- Week 3–4: small autoscaler change: add 10m grace window for pinned routes behind feature flag. Run internal load-cases.
- Week 5–8: roll out egress-checker script + console link; measure reduction in private-deploy tickets mentioning KMS/network.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Privacy vs. observability: how much request meta can be on by default for all tenants? Legal/Compliance needs to sign off.
- API ergonomics vs. simplicity: per-route toggles increase surface area; how do we avoid config sprawl?
- Rollback scope: when we detect a problematic change, should we automatically rollback for all affected customers or only cohorts that opt-in? (pref: cohort, but requires rapid cohort detection tagging)

Immediate CS playbook (copyable):
1) Ask customer for route id + timestamp + model id. If missing, return error payload with auto-telemetry-hints header link.
2) If issue is latency spike and recent deploys exist, toggle batch-window downshift and monitor 15m.
3) For private-onboard errors: run egress-checker and request support bundle; escalate to infra-privates with priority "onboarding-blocker".

Notes to product/eng:
- These are intentionally pragmatic — low-friction wins first. We can prepare a larger program next quarter on "resilient defaults" that bundles these patches.
- Jira seeds: CS-1287 (egress-checker), CS-1298 (auto-telemetry-hints), INFRA-482 (pin-safe-autoscale), UX-307 (console banner for cohort rollouts).

Unresolved items for next sync:
- Decide who owns the privacy review for default telemetry (legal + security).
- Agree on telemetry schema for the one-click help header (minimal fields only).
- Timeline for model pinning safety defaults in Dedicated vs. Hosted.

Appendix: quick logs and snippets (drop-in for support replies)
- "If you're seeing 502/timeouts after a recent model pin, could you enable trace-id in the request header (X-Trace-Enable: 1) and paste the trace id? If you can't enable tracing, run this (egress-checker.sh) and paste output.
- Minimal egress-checker snippet: curl -s https://controlplane.redwood.ai/health && curl -s https://kms.partner-provider/v1/keys/lookup || echo 'KMS unreachable'

End — next steps: review with SE leads (Priya/Diego) and schedule quick PR for auto-telemetry-hints this sprint.
